prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 — Change that works for you: building a fairer Britain

Core belief: Britain’s problems stem from power and wealth being hoarded at the top. The Liberal Democrats will hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing economic, social, political and financial power. After decades of red–blue, blue–red governments, they offer structural change, not tinkering.

Four steps to a fairer Britain

1) Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- No income tax on the first £10,000 earned: around £700 back for most, 3.6 million low earners/pensioners lifted out of income tax.
- Paid for by closing loopholes and asking the wealthy and polluters to pay a fair share: basic-rate relief only on pensions; align capital gains with income tax; anti‑avoidance measures; per‑plane aviation duty (with higher rates where rail exists); 1% mansion tax over £2m; reform non‑doms.
- Responsible deficit reduction, not ideology: over £15bn identified savings (e.g., scrap ID cards/biometric passports/Intercept Modernisation Programme; cap public sector pay rises at £400; banking levy; reform tax credits; end Child Trust Fund payments; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; prison reform). A cross‑party Council on Financial Stability to guide pace and scale.

2) A fair chance for every child
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium targeted at disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes, fund one‑to‑one tuition, and attract top teachers; more school freedom and teacher‑led standards via an independent Educational Standards Authority.
- Guarantee SEN assessments at 5; tackle bullying; widen 14–19 choices across academic/vocational routes; reform league tables.
- Scrap tuition fees, phased over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); reform bursaries; expand foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships.

3) A fair future: creating jobs by making Britain greener
- Break up the banks; get responsible lending going; curb bonuses; develop local/regional finance (Local Enterprise Funds, Regional Stock Exchanges).
- Green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; Eco Cash‑Back for home efficiency/micro‑generation; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage scheme.
- United Kingdom Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private capital for rail, energy and broadband.
- Climate leadership: zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; over 40% emissions cut by 2020; at least 40% electricity from clean sources by 2020 (rising to 100% by 2050); coal only with top‑tier CCS; reject new nuclear in favour of cheaper conservation/renewables; European Supergrid.
- Cancel Heathrow third runway; reform aviation tax to per‑plane duty.

4) A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties
- Fair votes (STV), fewer MPs, fixed‑term parliaments; fully elected second chamber; right to recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; end big‑money influence; written constitution via citizens’ convention.
- Freedom Bill: scrap ID cards; regulate CCTV; protect protest, free speech and libel reform; remove innocent DNA; stop mass retention of internet data; end control orders; 14‑day pre‑charge limit; allow intercept evidence.
- Devolve power and money: fair votes for local elections; return business rates to councils; local policing via elected authorities; elected Local Health Boards.

Public services and society
- NHS: cut waste, not frontline care; integrate health and social care; patient entitlements to timely diagnosis/treatment; GP choice (incl. email).
- Work and families: flexible working for all; shared parental leave; tackle pay discrimination; name‑blind recruitment and fair pay audits.
- Older people: restore earnings link with a “triple lock” floor of 2.5%; scrap forced retirement; more respite for carers; long‑term care commission.
- Housing/transport: insulate homes nationwide; energy‑efficient new builds; fair repossession rules; cut regulated rail fares in real terms; empower councils to regulate buses.

Britain in the world
- Pro‑Europe reformers; tougher global financial regulation; 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; human rights at the core; rule out like‑for‑like Trident replacement; defence review to meet modern threats; fair, firm immigration with exit checks, a National Border Force, regional points‑based work routes, an end to child detention, and earned citizenship for settled, law‑abiding families.
